sentence: Eight-year-old boy referred from the Ophthalmology clinic due to pruritic clustered vesicular-crusted periorbital and right eyelid lesions, diagnosed with eyelid herpes zoster that does not improve with topical acyclovir and tobramycin eye drops.

For this reason, the antiviral was replaced by its oral presentation, without experiencing improvement in six days, deciding then to withdraw the acyclovir and consult Dermatology, where topical zinc sulfate and sertaconazole were prescribed after collecting a skin culture, when labeling the periorbital lesion of tinea faciei and adding a topical corticosteroid to mitigate the hyperkeratotic and scaling component.

Three weeks later he went for a check-up, where a slight decrease in the itching was observed, with stagnation of the previous lesions, while still maintaining extensive peeling and keratosis with an ill-defined erythematovesicular base.

The culture is positive for Candida krusei, so previous therapies are withdrawn, recommending oral griseofulvin in two daily doses with fatty meals and suspending topical corticosteroid, producing an improvement in the condition with disappearance of skin signs in the following 14 days.
